entities.name: African Democratic Rally
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The African Democratic Rally (Rassemblement Démocratique Africain, RDA), founded in 1946 at Bamako under the leadership of Félix Houphouët-Boigny of Côte d'Ivoire, was the most important pan-African political party of the French decolonization era — the organization through which French West African political elites negotiated the terms of independence from France, eventually leading to the independence of 14 French African states between 1958 and 1960.

The RDA was founded immediately after France's 1946 constitution extended limited citizenship rights to African subjects, creating the first opportunity for organized African political participation in the French system. Houphouët-Boigny and other African leaders affiliated the RDA with the French Communist Party (PCF) for electoral and organizational support — a pragmatic alliance that brought intense colonial repression (the 1949-1950 RDA riots and the Bloody Dimbokro incident). In 1950 Houphouët-Boigny broke the PCF affiliation, shifting the RDA toward accommodation with the French government.

The RDA's most consequential moment was the 1958 constitutional referendum on De Gaulle's Fifth Republic, when Houphouët-Boigny advised African territories to vote 'Yes' for autonomy within the French Community rather than full independence. Only Guinea under Sékou Touré voted 'No' and received immediate independence and hostile French treatment. The remaining territories gained independence in 1960 — but largely as French-friendly states under leaders like Houphouët-Boigny who maintained close ties with France (Françafrique). The RDA thus shaped the character of Franco-African post-independence relations for decades.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The African Democratic Rally — the pan-African party that negotiated the independence of 14 French African states, shaped the Françafrique post-colonial relationship, and represented the most organized political force in French decolonization — is one of the most consequential political organizations in African history.
